The Gold Coin of France, Making an Allowance for the Remedy of the Mint, Contains 21 carats
and three-fourths of fine gold, and two carats one-fourth of alloy. The mark of standard gold,
therefore, is worth no more than about 671 livers ten deniers.
But in France, this mark of standard gold is coined into 30 Louis-Doors of 24 livers each,

raw_segments.text: Seigneurage in France raises the value of the coin higher than in proportion to the
quantity of pure gold which it contains. Thus, by the edict of January 1726, the mint price
of fine gold of 24 carats was fixed at 740 livers, 9 sues, and 1 denier, 1 eleventh,
the mark of 8 Paris ounces. See, Dictionnaire, Desmonies, Tom, Roman 2, Article Seigneurage,
P. 439, par 81. Abbot de Bazinghen, Conseiller-Commissaire en la Cour Desmonies a Paris. The gold coin
of France, making an allowance for the remedy of the mint, contains 21 carats and three-fourths of
fine gold and two carats one-fourth of alloy. The mark of standard gold, therefore, is worth no
more than about 671 livers, 10 deniers. But in France, this mark of standard gold is coined into
30 Louis-Dors of 24 livers each or into 720 livers. The coinage, therefore, increases the value of a
mark of standard gold bullion by the difference between 671 livers, 10 deniers, and 720 livers,
or by 48 livers, 19 sues, and 2 deniers.
